Kangaroos Secure Pool A Top Spot

Australia secured the top position in Pool A with a 66-6 victory over the Cook Islands in Townsville, according to match reports from the tournament. Despite the lopsided final scoreline, the performance highlighted ongoing areas of improvement for the Australian side as they head toward the knockout stages.

Standout Performances and Match Flow

Reece Walsh played a central role in the Australian attack, contributing a try and five try assists. Wingers Tom Trbojevic and Jack Bostock both scored hat-tricks, continuing strong scoring form through the group stage.

However, match reports noted that the Kangaroos struggled with consistency during periods of the game, committing 15 errors that interrupted their attacking momentum.

  • First-Half Struggles: The Cook Islands capitalized on early Australian mistakes, taking a brief lead following a converted try by hooker Rua Ngatikaura.
  • Second-Half Surge: Australia responded with a six-try blitz in the opening 20 minutes after halftime to pull away from the opposition.
  • Squad Depth: The Cook Islands fielded a lineup featuring experienced campaigners including Val Holmes and 37-year-old halfback Brad Takairangi, though depth challenges ultimately limited their sustained competitiveness.

Selection Decisions Ahead

Coach Kevin Walters faces looming selection choices ahead of the upcoming semi-final match against either Samoa or Tonga. Decisions regarding the fullback position between Walsh and James Tedesco remain a focal point for the coaching staff following this partly clunky display.
